facts.claim: The code's compass words contradict each other, so a designer cannot trust 'north' or 'south' in comments. Some files call -z north and +z south (the yard side). Others call +z north (the bay, the counterweight well, the facade crane, the midstack decks). This map uses the brief's convention: -z is north, toward the second tower.
facts.numbers: -z is north in summit.hpp: kDeckNorthZ -191.5 is less than kDeckSouthZ -183.5. +z is north in bay.hpp: kNorthZ -124 is greater than kSouthZ -133.

facts.claim: The code contradicts itself about which side of the 220 ring the hook rack stands on. physics_world.cpp calls it the 'north-west corner'. The probe code calls it the 'south band'. Its actual position is x -22.4, z -127.6: the +z (yard) side, away from the second tower.

The Stack's native frame is a 52 m square about (0, -150): x -26 to 26, z -176 to -124. Its decks sit every 11 m from 11 to 154 m, each 0.5 m thick with its top at level × 11. Its corner and mid-span columns are 1.6 m square at x or z ±26, so their north faces are at z -176.8. All of it carries entity kTowerEntityId, friction 0.85.

Only the UpperColumn corners (z -176.8, 154-165 m) and the UpperBrace diagonals in the face plane (z -176.2 to -175.8, 153.8-165.2 m) stand there. facts.claim: The yard crane's mast stands at x -66, z -137, with its slew ring at 58 m and a trolley range of 5-37 m from the mast. Its hook can reach only about z -174 at most, far short of the second tower or the mountain-cone foot at that x (about z -237).

facts.claim: The second tower's body is a static box x -76 to 16, z -370 to -290, y 0 to 1600, friction 0.8, entity kTowerEntityId (11). It is drawn as a single opaque concrete box with the same size and centre. Its facing side (+z, toward tower one) is the face at z -290. Its three other faces and its 92 × 80 m roof at 1600 m carry no relief.

Five FacePier boxes, each 6 × 460 × 3 m with centre at y 230 and z -290, half-buried in the face. They cover y 0 to 460, stand 1.5 m proud (front at z -288.5), and occupy x -71 to -65, -52 to -46, -33 to -27, -14 to -8, and 5 to 11. Each pier's top at y 460 exposes a flat 6 × 1.5 m area in front of the face.

Each therefore stands only 0.6 m proud of the face (front at z -289.4). Piers (1.5 m proud) and ducts (3.1 m) interrupt them, so each band's exposed top is a 0.6 m-deep ledge in segments between piers and ducts.

Four FaceDuct boxes, each 3 × 380 × 3 m, centred at x -60, -40, -20 and 0, y 200, z -288.4. They cover y 10 to 390 and z -289.9 to -286.9. Each stands 3.1 m proud of the face with a 0.1 m slot behind it. Each duct's top at y 390 is a flat 3 × 3 m area.
Four TimberCladding boxes, each 8 × 44 × 1.2 m, centred at x -58, -39, -21 and -2, y 62, z -289.2. They cover y 40 to 84 and z -289.8 to -288.6, standing 1.4 m proud with a 0.2 m slot behind.

facts.topic: tower two, facade: FaceDrum and lights
facts.claim: FaceDrum is listed in the exporter's SOLID set but nothing builds it, so it does not exist. The FloorLight bands (y 30-354) and FloorLightHigh bands (y 380-890) are non-solid. They are drawn at z -291.3 ± 0.3, which puts them 1.0-1.6 m inside the opaque mass, behind the face at z -290. They cannot be seen, so the second tower shows no lit floors, day or night.
facts.numbers: face_z - 1.3 = -291.3; a depth of 0.6 spans z -291.6 to -291.0, while the mass spans z -370 to -290.

facts.claim: A hold, for either the hook's bite or a hand's grip, must be a Box subshape. Its longest dimension must be at least 0.25 m, and both thinner dimensions at most 0.18 m. It must sit on a static body, or on a dynamic one of at least 400 kg; sensors are excluded. Convex hulls (mountains, trees, Part cylinders) are never holds, because leaf_box rejects anything that is not a Box.
No part of the second tower qualifies as a hook hold or hand grip. Every facade part, and the mass itself, has at least two dimensions far above the 0.18 m limit.
facts.numbers: Thinner dimensions (full sizes): Pier 6 × 3; Band 1.4 × 2; Duct 3 × 3; Cladding 8 × 1.2; Mass 92 × 80. Every one exceeds 0.18 m.

facts.claim: Nothing on the second tower can be climbed today. There are no holds. Its ledges are 16 m apart vertically (FaceBand pitch), while a wall climb gives at most 7 m/s of rise (about 2.5 m) and a mantle at most 1.85 m. The standable flats are the pier tops at 460 m (6 × 1.5 m each), the duct tops at 390 m (3 × 3 m) and the exposed cladding top at 84 m. Each is a dead end: the next band is 11.3 m above a pier top and 1.3 m below the 392 band above a duct top.

A FaceBand ledge is 0.6 m deep. The player capsule's radius is 0.35, so standing against the face leaves 0.25 m of band under the capsule's centre. But a climb-up's landing is placed kLandingInset (0.47 m) past the lip, which is only 0.13 m from the face, so a mantle onto a band is probably refused for lack of clearance. Whether a hang or a stand works was not run.
facts.numbers: 0.6 - 0.47 = 0.13 m, which is less than the 0.35 m radius.

facts.claim: The near mountain peaks are solid collision, not backdrop. Each is a 12-sided convex-hull cone with foot radius 0.62 × height. Three of them extend their skirts into the void and bury the second tower's foot: line 1015 at (-160, -610), height 640; line 1019 at (110, -630), height 700; line 1023 at (180, -540), height 600. A code comment calls the mountains non-collidable; the exporter's SOLID list contradicts it.
The cones bury the second tower's face (z -290) up to 80-111 m across its whole width. They also cover the tower's sides and back to much greater heights.
facts.numbers: Surface height at z -290 = the highest cone face over the point, computed from the exported hull points. x -76: 87.6; -60: 80.7; -40: 86.8; -30: 91.1; -20: 95.4; 0: 104.1; 16: 111.2. Along x -76 and x 16 respectively: z -330 gives 152.1 and 175.5; z -370 gives 216.6 and 240.0.

facts.claim: At grade, the cone foot crosses the void about 35-64 m north of the Stack's face. The walkable ground between the towers is a strip from z -176.8 to about z -212 (x 16) or z -234 to -240 (x -30 to -60). The rest of the void, northward, is cone.
The cone faces cannot be stood on. Every face is 59.1° (surface normal y 0.514). Support needs normal y ≥ 0.55 (about 56.6°). The creases between cones measured about 58.2°.
facts.numbers: tan θ = height / (0.62 × height × cos 15°) gives 59.1°, and cos 59.1° = 0.514. The crease between cones 1015 and 1019 sits near x -57 and rises 8.1 m per 5 m.

facts.claim: The FaceBands at 40, 56 and 72 m lie entirely inside the cones. The band at 88 m is exposed only from x -75 to -33.5, and the band at 104 m from x -75 to 3.5; from 120 m up the bands are fully exposed. Only the westmost TimberCladding (x -62 to -54) stands above the cone, its 84 m top 4.7-6.5 m clear. The other claddings, and the feet of every pier and duct, are buried.
facts.numbers: Cone height at the cladding fronts (z -288.6): x -62 to -54: 77.5-79.3; x -43 to -35: 83.2-86.7; x -25 to -17: 91-94.5; x -6 to 2: 99-103. Cone height at the pier fronts: 81.7 / 80.5 / 88.7 / 96.9 / 105.1. At the duct fronts: 75.7 / 81.8 / 90.4 / 99.1.

facts.claim: Grade is native: a box x -240 to 240, z -300 to 180, top y 0, friction 0.6. The valley floor beyond it has its top at y -0.3. The second tower's front 10 m (z -300 to -290) rest on grade. Its rear 70 m float 0.3 m above the valley floor, but all of that lies inside the cones.

Inside the void between the two towers' x spans there are no trees, fences or other solids at grade. Only the buttresses stand near the Stack's corners. The nearest trees are west of x -95: trunks at (-99.5, -212.8), (-106.1, -209.7), (-115.0, -182.7) and (-140.2, -238.4), canopies up to 15.6 m. A player can walk from the yard round the Stack into the void's floor but is stopped by the 59° cones short of the tower's foot. A native test already proves walking into such rock ends against it.

From the ground today, the second tower cannot be reached or climbed. Its foot is buried under 80-111 m of rock that cannot be stood on and offers no holds. Hulls are never holds. The facade parts that are exposed start at about 75-111 m and themselves offer no holds.

The towers are offset. The second tower's centre (-30, -330) lies 30 m west (-x) and 180 m north (-z) of tower one's axis (0, -150). That is 182.5 m centre to centre. Tower one's centreline x = 0 meets the second tower's face 76 m from its west edge and 16 m from its east edge.

The x overlap between the towers is large and shrinks as tower one tapers. The second tower spans x -76 to 16. From 340 m up, tower one's main frame lies almost entirely within that span, apart from its east edge where it exceeds 16.

The clear horizontal gap, measured along z from tower one's northmost floor edge to the second tower's nearest collidable surface at the same height, is 110.9-131.3 m. The summit and derrick reduce it to 89.4-98.5 m. Above about 111 m nothing collidable stands in the void.

The owner's 30-61 m range can be met only by moving a structure. With the second tower where it is, the clear gap is 89-131 m. If its face moved south to z -230 to -240, cones would bury its foot only up to about 0-45 m, instead of 80-111 m today. Moving it therefore changes what is reachable from the ground.

No hook shot can cross the void. The line is at most 30 m and every gap is at least 89.4 m. Nothing stands in the void above about 111 m to bite on: the cones are hulls, never holds, and lie behind the second tower's face at those heights.

The parachute is always carried and opens whenever the player is airborne. It applies quadratic drag k = 0.1211 to the full velocity, giving about 9 m/s terminal speed against a lethal impact speed of 20 m/s. Air control still steers toward the take-off's horizontal speed at up to 14 m/s². The parachute therefore produces a real glide.
facts.numbers: Equilibrium solves 0.1211 × |v| × vy = 9.81. For horizontal 5.5 / 8 / 9 m/s, the descent is 8.20 / 7.42 / 7.08 m/s, a glide of 0.67 / 1.08 / 1.27. Horizontal drag is 6.6 / 10.6 / 12.5 m/s², below the 14 m/s² of air control, so the speed holds. Computed, not run.

facts.claim: By that computation, a player who jumps from tower one's upper decks and opens the parachute reaches the second tower's face somewhere between about 290 and 725 m. The pier tops at 460 m and duct tops at 390 m could be landed on at below the 20 m/s lethal speed. The second tower is therefore probably already reachable by air today, ending at a dead-end ledge.
facts.numbers: Arrival height = start - gap / glide, for glides 0.67 / 1.08 / 1.27. Summit 802.64 with a 98.5 m gap: 655.6 / 711.4 / 725.1. 750 deck with 128 m: 559 / 632 / 649. 662 deck with 128 m: 471 / 544 / 561. 484 ring with 127.7 m: 294 / 366 / 384. The delay before opening and the steering are ignored.

facts.claim: Only two wind zones exist. One is off the west face (x ≤ -26.6, 262-300 m, z -166 to -128). The other is over the summit arm (x ≤ -12, 788-830 m, z -197 to -178). The void between the towers has no wind.

main_world.gd _build_tower_skin builds the second tower's relief and then calls _build_stack_continuation. That function builds tower one's UpperColumn, UpperDeck, UpperBrace and UpperLightBand from 154 to 418 m. The ring decks at 176-396 m that the route stands on exist only as UpperDeck world solids from that call. Deleting or moving _build_tower_skin without keeping the call deletes tower one's rings.

kTowerEntityId (11) belongs to both the second tower's mass and every native Stack deck and column. body_id_for_entity(kTowerEntityId) returns the second tower's body, so support-velocity lookups made while standing on any Stack deck resolve to the mass. Both are static, so this is harmless today, but it is wrong if either ever moves. Native tests assert support == kTowerEntityId on Stack decks.

The TowerMass entry in world_solids.inc mirrors the native body. The loader skips it only if its world bounds match an owned body within 0.02 m. world_solids.inc is generated from the Godot builders, and CI regenerates it and fails on any difference. The facade's position comes from local variables in _build_tower_skin (mass_x -30, face_z -290), not from the native constants. Relocating the second tower means changing physics_world.cpp:65-71, main_world.gd:69 and main_world.gd:521-522 together, then regenerating world_solids.inc.

A native test requires more than 1,400 world-solid bodies, at least one recognised mirror and no rejected hulls. The body-order test snapshots the world-solid count. Adding or removing solids or native bodies shifts body order and the save layout, which is why native builders append new bodies last.
kTowerHeightMeters (1600) sizes the second tower's native body. The bridge also exposes it as get_tower_height_meters, and Godot prints it in proof lines and context.

The engineering and product authorities forbid authoring a second tower, and the start file says no route exists above the 750 deck. The TDD's work order 008 says 'Do not author a second tower', and its architecture-rejection tests reject a proposal that 'authors a second tower ... instead of amending this tree'. The GDD says downstream work must not author a second tower. The start file says 'Above the 750 deck no route is built: only the neighbouring shaft's mass'. That is stale: the summit exists.

The Matron can hear the player at all only inside a hard-coded tower-one footprint: |x| < 27 and -177 < z < -123, plus her climbs and joined decks. A player on or crossing to the second tower (z < -286.9) is outside it.

The zipline system caps at 24 lines. The world already attempts up to 24: one yard line, 13 across the Stack's well and 10 up the rings. A void-crossing zipline would be refused unless the cap is raised. Each line is also swept against the built world and needs a floor under both ends.

The camera's far plane is 2600 m, with fov 82 and near 0.05. The second tower's farthest corner, (-76, 1600, -370), is about 1642 m from the yard spawn, so the whole tower is always inside the far plane. No visibility range, LOD or shadow setting singles the second tower out.

All static dressing, the second tower included, is merged into distance batches. A near batch (lit by lamps, bump-mapped, casting shadows) is drawn only while the camera is within 260 m (plus a 20 m fade) of its 192 m far section's centre. Beyond that a plain vertex-coloured far batch is drawn, with no lamps and no shadow. The TowerMass's single part is centred at y 800, so its far section's centre is (-96, 864, -288): it is the far version from the yard and the 154 deck, and the near version from about the 750 deck.
facts.numbers: Distance to (-96, 864, -288): from the yard (0, 1.7, 0) about 915 m; from the 154 deck (0, 155, -171.5) about 725 m; from the 750 deck (0, 751, -150) about 202 m. The facade parts' far sections are centred at y 96 (bands and cladding below 192 m), y 288 (piers, ducts, bands at 192-384 m) and y 480 (bands above 384 m), at x -96 or 96, z -288.

facts.claim: Static parts whose longest dimension is 1.5 m or less are drawn only within 160 m (plus 20 m) of their 96 × 48 × 96 m section, and cast no shadow. Short rungs or bars added to the second tower would therefore vanish at the 110-131 m void distances once section offsets are counted. Moving kit bodies are drawn only to 40 × their largest extent (clamped to 120-1200 m) unless whitelisted as far-visible. Only the summit frame and the yard crane statics are whitelisted.

The environment fog is exponential at density 0.00022, with height fog below 90 m (height density 0.0004), aerial perspective 0.18 and sky affect 0.2. Across the void at height the second tower reads nearly unfogged, about 3% at 128 m. Only its foot and the cones sit in the height fog.

The sun's shadow distance is 120, 160, 220 or 300 m by quality level (220 in the scene). The second tower's face, 110-131 m away, falls within shadow range at the medium level and above, but only while its near batch is drawn.

The cloud layer is a presentation-only band of 168 drifting puffs between 455 and 505 m. Each puff is 80-130 m across, times a scale of 0.8-1.5. They are kept only 75 m clear of tower one's axis (0, -150); nothing keeps them off the second tower. Puffs therefore pass through the void and through the second tower between about 455 and 505 m. A puff fades as the eye comes inside it, and puffs have no collision.
facts.numbers: The second tower's face is 140 m from tower one's axis and its centre 182.5 m, both inside the cloud annulus of 75-950 m.

facts.claim: No lamp reaches the second tower. The tower-foot floods reach 48 m from the Stack's base, and the yard's sodium floods 26 m. Its only emissive dressing, the floor-light bands, is buried inside the mass. At night it is lit only by the sky, the sun or moon and the fill light. The summit frame is drawn at any distance.
The second tower (1600 m) is about twice tower one's top (802.64 m deck). From the summit, its face is 98.5 m away and its roof 797 m higher.
facts.numbers: atan(797 / 98.5) = 83° up from the summit; from the 154 deck, atan(1444 / 114) = 85.5°.

risks: The near-peak mountain cones are solid collision and fill the void's north half. A design that puts anything at the second tower's foot, or expects to walk to it, must reshape those cones (main_world.gd:690-703). That also changes the drawn mountains (the carved mesh stays inside each cone), the hull table, body order and the CI drift diff.

_build_tower_skin also calls _build_stack_continuation, which builds the ring decks at 176-396 m that the route stands on (world solids only). Editing, moving or removing the skin function can delete tower one's rings silently.

kTowerEntityId is shared by the second tower's mass and every Stack deck and column, and body_id_for_entity maps it to the mass. Give anything new or moving on the second tower its own entity id. Stack tests assert support == kTowerEntityId.

Relocating the second tower means changing three places together: the native box (physics_world.cpp:65-71), the drawn box (main_world.gd:69) and the facade's mass_x and face_z locals (main_world.gd:521-522). Then regenerate world_solids.inc. If the TowerMass mirror misses by more than 0.02 m, a duplicate body appears.

The parachute is always carried and probably already lets a player glide from the 484-802 m levels to the second tower's face and land on a pier top (460 m) or duct top (390 m) without dying. Any 'first access only through tower one' design must account for this. It is computed, not run.
The hook's 30 m line cannot span any gap of 89-131 m, and nothing in the void above about 111 m can be bitten. A crossing needs new architecture or a long-span mechanism, not the hook alone.

The gap is not uniform. The frame tapers, so the gap widens from about 111 m at 154 m to about 131 m at 572 m and holds at 128 m on the 640-750 decks. The summit and derrick protrude to 89-98.5 m. The owner's 30-61 m needs a structure moved or built out about 50-80 m.

Moving the second tower closer, with its face near z -230 to -240, would bring its foot out of the cones (0-45 m buried instead of 80-111 m). The ground could then reach it unless new architecture blocks it.

Holds the size of a hand (1.5 m or shorter) added to the second tower are drawn only within about 160-180 m of their section, so they may be invisible from tower one. Moving kit bodies (cars, gondolas) are drawn to only 40 × their extent unless whitelisted far-visible like the summit frame.

For most of the climb the second tower is drawn as a flat, vertex-coloured far batch with no lamps and no shadows. New detail on it inherits this unless it is moved into a near batch or made far-visible.
Code comments use 'north' for both +z and -z. Designers should work in raw coordinates.

The governance documents explicitly forbid 'a second tower' (TDD :909, :933; GDD :608), and the start file says nothing exists above the 750 deck. The owner must amend them, or the work fails the TDD's own architecture-rejection test.
The Matron's hearing footprint is hard-coded to tower one (matron.cpp:1615). If the second tower is her place, her senses and level model will not see it.
The summit deck, derrick mast and crown frame have nothing under them in code. A bridge or tie that assumes structure beneath the summit has nothing to land on.
The zipline cap of 24 is already used by up to 24 attempted lines. A crossing zipline needs the cap raised, and the next free entity ids come after 1800 + 24.
Adding native bodies or world solids changes body order and the save layout (sim_tests_body_order.cpp). The existing code appends late bodies last, with comments, to keep saves aligned.
The floor-light bands meant to light the second tower are buried 1.0-1.6 m inside the mass. If the facade is rebuilt with face_z changed, they may suddenly appear, or remain invisible.
Clouds pass through the second tower and the void at 455-505 m. A crossing or ledge in that band will be fogged by puffs. They are presentation only: no collision and no wind.
The FaceBand ledges are 0.6 m deep. A mantle's landing inset (0.47 m) leaves 0.13 m from the wall, so climbing up onto them is probably refused; hanging and standing were not tested.
unknowns: Whether the movement code lets a player hang on, stand on or mantle onto a 0.6 m FaceBand ledge, or land on a 1.5 m pier top, was not run.
The parachute's arrival heights are equilibrium computations. The delay before opening, the transient, contact with the wall and landing recovery on a 1.5 m ledge were not simulated.
How many of the 24 zipline attempts actually fit and are built cannot be told from the source alone.

How far the drawn, carved rock lies below the cone collision surface at the second tower's face, above the true foot band (77-84 m), was not measured. There may be an invisible collision band up to 80-111 m.

Native kit bodies were surveyed from each band's frame code and from a search for literal z values north of -177, not by dumping the built world. A computed-coordinate body further north is unlikely but not ruled out.
Whether the derrick's chain-pit slab at 776 m (x 14.4-17.6, z -200.6 to -197.4) is reachable or standable under its ballast is unknown.
Godot's exact fog formula on the mobile renderer, and the camera's keep_aspect (whether the 82° fov is vertical or horizontal), were not checked.
The yard crane jib's physical length beyond the trolley's 37 m reach was not read; it is irrelevant to the void at its 58 m height, but unverified.
Whether puff placement after wrapping can put cloud quads within the second tower's volume at a given time was established only from the annulus rule, not observed.

facts.claim: The native steps at 90 Hz (1/90 s per tick) under Jolt's default gravity of 9.81 m/s^2; nothing in src/sim calls SetGravity.

The player is a dynamic capsule 1.8 m tall (radius 0.35, half-height 0.9), 85 kg, zero friction, zero linear damping, rotation locked. Crouched it is 1.2 m (half-height 0.6) with the soles kept where they were.
facts.numbers: kCrouchDrop = 0.9 - 0.6 = 0.3 m

facts.claim: The body has no air drag (mLinearDamping 0, and no drag term except the parachute), so a fall keeps speeding up until it lands.
facts.numbers: from 800 m: v = sqrt(2*9.81*800) = 125 m/s with no chute

facts.claim: Walking tops out at 5.5 m/s relative to the support. Ground traction is 22 m/s^2, so the body reaches full speed in 0.25 s. Traction scales with the slope (the normal's y) and with landing balance (.25 + .75 b).

Sprint runs at 8.0 m/s. It needs Sprint held, the stick at 0.7 or more and within 45 degrees of the facing, the body standing with empty hands and off a beam, not limping, and balance at 0.8 or more. A sprint kept up gathers toward 9.0 m/s (flow) at 0.6 m/s^2.
Crouch-walking runs at 2.475 m/s. A limp also caps the stride at 2.475 m/s with no sprint. Walking a beam runs at 2.0 m/s.
A free load in the hands caps speed at 1 - m*g/720 N times the stride, so the cap reaches 0 at 73.4 kg. There is no sprint while carrying, and no vault, mantle or hang begins. A jump is not refused.

A jump sets the vertical speed to 5.5 m/s over the support's. Apex rise is 1.54 m (the code comment says 1.51 m measured) and flat airtime is 1.12 s (comment: 1.111 s measured). The run's horizontal speed is kept.

On the flat, a walking jump carries 6.2 m, a sprint jump 9.0 m and a flow jump 10.1 m, ignoring the capsule radius. Onto a landing 1.2 m higher the flight is 0.825 s (6.6 m at a sprint). Onto one 2 m lower it is 1.41 s (11.3 m at a sprint).

In the air the stick steers at 14 m/s^2 toward stick x air_full_speed_. air_full_speed_ is max(5.5, the horizontal speed the body had on its last ground tick or traversal exit). With the stick let go in a committed flight, only gravity acts.

A jump still goes for 0.1 s after walking off an edge (rising under 4.5 m/s, falling under 1.5 m/s). A press made 0.1 s before landing is kept. A second Jump within 0.3 s of takeoff asks for the vault the takeoff could have been.
facts.numbers: 9 ticks, 9 ticks, 27 ticks at 90 Hz

facts.claim: A sighted landing is offered from 0.8 to 4.5 m ahead, up to 1.2 m up or 2.0 m down, from a look cast of 9 m. Jump then sets the horizontal speed that lands the feet there, changed from the run's by at most 3 m/s and never over 8 m/s. A landing within 0.5 m of the point counts as prepared.
facts.numbers: standing reach at most 3 m/s * flight: 3.36 m flat, 2.47 m onto +1.2 m (the code comment says ~1.5 m: see unknowns); 0.35 + 0.15 = 0.5 m

facts.claim: An edge under 0.35 m is walked up. A vault takes a 0.35-1.15 m rise, crosses 1.30 m and lands up to 1.40 m below the takeoff in 0.38 s. A mantle takes a 0.35-1.85 m rise in 0.42 s. Both need the face within 0.95 m of the capsule's skin (1.30 m from the centre).

At 6 m/s or more a vault is taken from 0.25 s of travel ahead (at most 2 m) and keeps the run's speed up to flow's 9 m/s. At 4.5 m/s or more, Jump at a 0.35-1.15 m top with 0.5 m of depth, within 0.18 s of the run, plants a foot and jumps from the top, keeping 92% of the run's speed. A rider leaving a mantle at a run keeps the run's speed less 1.5 m/s.

In flight from a jump at 4.5 m/s or more, within about 40 degrees of a wall beside the body, with the stick not turned away and the body falling, a foot plants every 0.222 s, at most 3 times a flight. Each plant pushes 1.2 m/s off the wall and removes up to 0.96 m/s of fall. It never lifts the body.

Jumped square at a wall (within 30 degrees, at least 3 m/s into it, the stick at it) that stands above the hands' reach, the run turns upward at up to 7 m/s, once a flight. A jump while on the wall kicks off: 3 m/s out, up to 2 m/s along the wall where the stick points (the tic-tac), and 2.4 m/s more up. At most 4 kicks a flight.

In the air, with the stick within about 72 degrees of the facing, the hands close on a lip 0.45-1.35 m above the body's centre (1.35-2.25 m above the soles), within 1.30 m ahead, with a supported landing on top. They close while falling, or while rising at up to 2.5 m/s in a jump (0.2 m/s otherwise). Not within 0.3 s of a let-go, not crouched, not carrying.
facts.numbers: stick dot facing >= 0.3; 27-tick regrab lockout (tuning:593)

facts.claim: A hang has no time limit and nothing drains it. The arms are a tension spring (2 Hz, damping 1, stop at 0.538 m), and the hands slip only when the load stays over 4.5 kN for 14 ticks (0.156 s) or the impulse over 4.5 kN passes 350 N s. A torn catch breaks the right arm. One good arm holds half of both limits.
evidence: grep for stamina/fatigue in src/sim found nothing
facts.numbers: arm stop = 0.6 - 9.81/(2*pi*2)^2 = 0.538 m. Measured in the tuning comment: a catch after a 1 m fall holds (~170 N s over); after 6 m (10.9 m/s) it tears (~700 N s)

facts.claim: From a hang: Jump or Up climbs over the lip (a mantle). The stick sideways shimmies at 0.6 m/s while the lip runs on within 0.15 m of height. The body stills its own swing with up to 300 N. DROP lets go. On the ground, DROP with an edge 0.25-0.9 m behind and a drop of at least 1.5 m lowers the body into a hang over 0.6 s.

A bar overhead, 0.8-1.4 m above the centre, is caught in flight and hung from. A push along the swing kips with up to 160 N. Held forward, the free hand takes the next bar within 1.0 m of the shoulders, at least 0.3 m further on and not below them, no sooner than 0.3 s after the last regrip; failing a bar, a lip in the same reach. A broken arm cannot go hand over hand.
facts.numbers: catch aim 1.10 +/- 0.30 m above the centre; dead-hang reach to a bar 1 m on is 1.14 m, out of reach: the swing carries the body

facts.claim: Jump in the front half of a bar swing (moving the way the body faces, faster than 0.5 m/s) adds 2 m/s at 45 degrees forward-up as the hands open. Otherwise the body lets go with its swing velocity, and air_full_speed_ is set to that horizontal speed.
facts.numbers: +1.41 m/s forward, +1.41 m/s up

facts.claim: Climbing moves 0.9 m/s up, 1.2 m/s down and 0.6 m/s across, with gravity off, only onto holds the hands find. Crouch held is the fireman's slide at up to 4.5 m/s. Jump off pushes 4 m/s up and 2.5 m/s back, or 3.5 m/s along the structure where the stick points. Climbing up a ledge in reach tops out into a mantle (0.35-1.85 m rise). One good arm climbs at half speed.
facts.numbers: jump-off rise 4^2/(2*9.81) = 0.82 m

facts.claim: A hold is a Box leaf shape whose two thinner dimensions are each at most 0.18 m and whose length is at least 0.25 m, on a static body or a dynamic body of at least 400 kg. Cylinders and capsules are never holds, for hands or hook, because leaf_box accepts only Box sub-shapes.

A support narrower than 0.5 m and at least 1.5 m long, with no ground within 0.35 m below either side, is walked at 2.0 m/s and held on its line. Sideways stick under 0.8 leans; 0.8 or more steps off. Across the beam the body is an inverted pendulum whose centre of pressure stays within half the width plus 0.12 m. An extrapolated centre of mass past that falls off.

At 6 m/s or more toward an edge with the stick not driving that way, once the extrapolated centre of mass passes the edge the feet brake at only 8.3 m/s^2 (stick pulled back) or 5.0 m/s^2 (let go). Below 6 m/s a let-go stick stops at the ordinary 22 m/s^2.

Crouching at 5 m/s or more within 45 degrees of the facing slides in the 1.2 m capsule. Friction removes 3.43 m/s^2 (also on slopes, braked as on the flat). The stick steers at 2 m/s^2. The slide ends at 2.475 m/s.
Crouch while rising, or falling no faster than 1 m/s, draws the legs up (the short capsule, head where it was). Pressed while falling faster it readies a prepared landing or roll instead.

A landing's legs take up to 6 m/s of vertical speed free, or 8 m/s with Crouch held at contact (prepared). Above that the balance debt grows with the normal energy past the free part, to 0.9 at the lethal speed (times 0.6 if prepared), plus a quarter of the tangential energy if sliding across the facing at 3 m/s or more (a stumble). Traction then scales by .25 + .75b and reachable speed by .45 + .55b. Recovery takes 0.15 + 0.06*(v - free) s, clamped to 0.15-2 s.

A roll needs Crouch held at contact, at least 2.5 m/s forward within about 45 degrees of the facing (dot >= 0.7), at least 5 m/s of normal speed, and a clear, supported lane for the crouched capsule. It keeps the forward speed (braked 3 m/s^2) for 0.6 s and leaves a quarter of the debt. A blocked lane ends it as a heavy landing.

A genuine landing (not in a traversal or takeoff) whose world vertical speed just before contact is over 20 m/s kills. The rule uses only the world vertical component, not the speed relative to the support, so horizontal speed never makes a landing lethal.
facts.numbers: 20^2/(2*9.81) = 20.4 m of free fall from rest

facts.claim: A landing at a normal speed of 12 m/s breaks an ankle when planted, 14 m/s when prepared and 16 m/s when rolled. The break is a 30 s limp: stride x0.45, no sprint, jump x0.6. Hands climb, hang and swing as before.
facts.numbers: drops 7.34 m / 9.99 m / 13.05 m; limp jump 3.3 m/s, a 0.555 m rise

facts.claim: Any contact that is not a floor (contact normal from player to other with y >= -0.5) with a closing speed of 10 m/s or more kills, side-on. From 6 m/s it is a felt hit. From 8.5 m/s it breaks the arm on the side the blow came from, for 30 s (climb x0.5, grip x0.5, no hand over hand). Corpses, sensors and the Matron's body are not blows.
facts.numbers: 10 m/s = a 5.1 m fall

facts.claim: On a death the native leaves a corpse at the death, then restores the player to the committed checkpoint position (its centre, crouched if committed crouched) at zero velocity. Every kit body, the slingshot, the swing, the vertical machines, the Matron and the bay go back to the checkpoint. All zipline trolleys are re-parked. The parachute is stowed, injuries are healed, the hook comes back stowed (kept if had), and regrab is locked out for 27 ticks.

A checkpoint commits every tick the body is grounded, outside a traversal, alive, with a ray from its centre meeting a walkable surface (normal y >= 0.55) within the half-height plus 0.15 m. Designers do not place checkpoints: any firm standable surface becomes one. There is no dwell timer.

The only thing that stops checkpoint renewal is the Matron. While she is out and alive and the player is on her deck (or a deck tied to it), commits stop. The one at her burst-out is committed on the first firm tick after it.

Her hands within 0.85 m of the player kill only at her fully-changed stage, as a lethal fall does (corpse, restore). At lower stages they shove at 5.5 m/s along the floor and 2 m/s up, once every 1.5 s. A dangerous-stage shove aims at the shaft's rim within 3 m. She hunts at 6.8 m/s and throws stock at 7.5 m/s.

A death leaves a ragdoll of 11 capsule parts (84 kg in all) moving as the body was. Corpses meet the static world, the climber and each other, never machines. At most 8 lie in the world (the oldest is dropped), and they are not saved.

The parachute is always carried, never found or lost. Its button toggles it, but only while airborne (the toggle is ignored on the tick after the body stood). There is no minimum height and no opening delay: drag acts from the next airborne tick.

The canopy is quadratic drag on the whole velocity vector, a = -0.1211*|v|*v, with no lift. Straight down it is terminal at 9.0 m/s. It is applied only outside a traversal and harness, so it also acts during a hook swing (traversal None) if left open.

Under the canopy, air control (14 m/s^2 toward stick x air_full_speed_) outpulls the drag, so a body that left the ground at speed v holds about v forward. Steady state with the stick forward: off a walk 5.4 m/s forward and 8.2 m/s sink (glide 0.66); off a sprint 7.9 and 7.4 (1.06); off flow speed 8.9 and 7.1 (1.25). With the stick let go: 9.0 m/s straight down.
facts.numbers: tick simulation in the code's order: air control, then drag, then gravity, dt 1/90

facts.claim: Because the canopy opens instantly, little height is needed. Opened at 30 m/s falling, it brings the body under the 20 m/s lethal speed in 3.9 m, under 12 m/s in 10.6 m, and to 9.5 m/s in 18.5 m. Opened at 50 m/s: 8.4 m, 15.1 m, 23.0 m.

Landing stows it automatically (any grounded tick). A harness (slingshot, swing seat, trapeze) and a death also stow it. Landing at the 9 m/s terminal is over the 6 m/s free (and 8 m/s prepared) limit, a small heavy-landing debt, but under the 12 m/s ankle break. A roll is possible with crouch held and at least 2.5 m/s forward.
While thrown by the slingshot until the next ground contact, the stick is a 2 m/s^2 force, not air control. Under the canopy that steers only about 1.8 m/s horizontally.
facts.numbers: k*|V|*vh = 2 and k*|V|*vy = 9.81 give vy = 8.9, vh = 1.8 m/s

facts.claim: The CHUTE button is offered only when airborne outside a traversal and either already open, falling faster than 6.5 m/s, or descending in slingshot flight. The HUD shows OPEN THE CHUTE in red at danger >= 0.6 (falling 12 m/s or faster, danger = -vy/20).

In the game the hook is a gun kit body on a rack whose base is at (-22.4, 220.25, -127.6), the gun at y 221.38. TAKE HOOK works within 1.6 m of the gun (centre to centre). Once taken the gun is parked (disabled) and the hook is kept through deaths, saves and loads. The rack stands on the +z (yard) side of tower one, about 162 m from the second shaft's z = -290 face.
facts.numbers: |-127.6 - (-290)| = 162.4 m; to the most proud relief (FaceDuct, z -286.9): 159.3 m

facts.claim: Fire works only with the hook stowed and the body outside a traversal (not hanging, climbing, swinging or on a zipline), on the ground or in the air. A 1.5 kg sphere (radius 0.08) launches from chest + 0.3 m up + 0.65 m along the aim, at the body's velocity plus 40 m/s along the aim. It flies under gravity as a real body (LinearCast) on a tension-only line of 30 m from the chest (chest = centre + 0.3 m).

Each tick the hook in flight bites the first hold whose box overlaps a 0.16 m sphere at its centre. It bites on contact, or on a near pass that ends a tick within 0.16 m. Anything else it glances off. With no bite in 2.5 s it is reeled in. On a bite the line is set to min(30 m, chest-to-bite distance) and anchored at the closest point on the hold's axis.

From a standing point a hold can be bitten if its straight-line distance from the chest (soles + 1.2 m) is at most 30 m. Across reach by height of the hold above the chest: 0 m up, 30.0 m; 10 m up, 28.3 m; 20 m up, 22.4 m; 25 m up, 16.6 m; 28 m up, 10.8 m; 30 m up, 0. Every metre of height difference comes out of the same 30 m.
facts.numbers: across <= sqrt(30^2 - h^2)

facts.claim: The aim is the camera's forward vector, sent every frame while the hook is had. The hook's 40 m/s flight drops under gravity: 0.31 m over 10 m (aim 1.8 degrees high), 1.23 m over 20 m (3.5 degrees), 2.76 m over 30 m (5.3 degrees). The HUD draws only a reticle dot: no hook trajectory, range or hold marker.

Across a thin hold the bite window is roughly the hold's section plus about 0.16 m (the hook's radius twice), at most about 0.34 m. At 30 m that is an angular tolerance of about 0.3-0.65 degrees. Look turns 0.003 rad per canvas unit of drag at sensitivity 1, so it is about 2-4 units of thumb drag. Gyro aim exists but defaults off.

Held, the reel first takes up slack at once (the line length is set to the current chest-to-anchor distance), then winds in at 3 m/s with at most 1200 N. Past that it stalls and holds. It lifts the body (1200 N > 834 N weight), but cannot tear it off a hold. Let go, it holds the length. The shortest line is 1 m.
facts.numbers: net lift (1200 - 85*9.81)/85 = 4.3 m/s^2; 30 m of line takes 10 s

facts.claim: On a taut line (tension > 30 N) in the air, the stick only pumps: up to 160 N horizontally along the stick while the body moves that way or is nearly still. There is no air control. With the line slack, ordinary air control applies. On the ground a line taking weight reduces the soles' traction in proportion.

Let go (request_hook_release, DROP or swipe-down) removes the line and the hook. The body keeps its velocity. stow_hook does not update air_full_speed_, so a stick held after a fast hook swing steers toward the last ground value (at least 5.5 m/s) at 14 m/s^2.
evidence: grep 'air_full_speed_ =' src/sim: only movement.cpp:910, traversal.cpp:587/769, climb.cpp:783, state.cpp:295

facts.claim: The tines hold up to 6 kN. Over that for 14 ticks they walk off, and an impulse over 6 kN past 500 N s tears them out. Either way the hook springs back 0.35 m along the line at 6 m/s and flies again: it may re-bite or is reeled in. A slack line caught by a fall tears at about 6.7 m/s of speed along the line (about 2.3 m of free fall); swinging on a taut line never comes near.
facts.numbers: one-tick catch: (85*v - 6000/90) > 500 gives v > 6.67 m/s; v^2/(2g) = 2.27 m. The comment says about 2.5 m

facts.claim: Where the straight line from the chest to its anchor would pass through a static body or one of 400 kg or more, it catches on that edge, 3 cm off the face. Up to 8 bends; past that the line runs straight through, counted as refused. The rope beyond a bend lies still. Reel and swing work only the free length from the chest to the nearest bend. Total rope out (free plus laid) never exceeds 30 m, and swung back round a bend it comes off.
facts.numbers: free length below a bend = 30 - laid length

facts.claim: While bitten the hook stays on as the body hangs or climbs; nothing stows it on a traversal. In the air, the hands still catch any ledge, hold or bar the stick points at (try_begin_hang runs every non-jump tick). A short drop over a deck lip on a taut line holds the body hanging below the lip, and the reel winds it back up.

facts.topic: pendulum carry on a 30 m line
facts.claim: Starting from rest with the bite at chest height 30 m away, a swing passes 30 m under the bite at 24.3 m/s (line pull 2.5 kN, 3 g) and rises to the same height 60 m from the start. Generally the same-height span is 2*sqrt(30^2 - H^2) for a bite H above the chest: 56.6 m at H = 10, 44.7 m at H = 20. Released at the best moment (no air control, no pumping), it carries 80.8 m to land 10 m lower (arriving at 11.2 m/s horizontal, 8.4 m/s down), 92.4 m to land 20 m lower (14.2 and 13.9), and 101.8 m to land 30 m lower (15.9 and 18.3: an ankle break).
facts.numbers: ideal pendulum: v_b = sqrt(2gL(1 - cos th0)); T_b = mg(3 - 2cos th0); release angle scanned in 0.1-degree steps

facts.claim: A line is one static kit body: top post 4.8 m over its floor, bottom post 3.4 m, a 1.2 m stand under the parked bar with a 2.4 m ramp, and a cable cylinder of radius 0.015 m. It is built only where both posts stand on static floor, the line is at least 10 m long, it drops at least 1 m, a 1 x 2.7 m box of hanging room sweeps clear along it, and it keeps clear of machines and reserved ground. There is no maximum length. At most 24 lines.

A jump from the stand into the parked bar (hands within 0.45 m, the bar at least 0.75 m above the centre, falling no faster than 3.5 m/s) clips the hands to a trolley. The slope drives it against 12 N of rolling drag. The stick held back squeezes a hand brake of up to 900 N. The last 3 m is a buffer at 4.9 m/s^2 over the slope's drive. At or under 5.4 m/s the buffer stops the rider. Faster, the stop's jolt tears the hands off (measured 6.5-9 m/s), with ledge-grip limits and a broken arm on a wrench, and the body is thrown on into the bottom post.

A 100 m or longer line is allowed by the code. There is no air drag, so the along-line acceleration is g*drop/length - 0.14 m/s^2. Unbraked, a 114 m horizontal line dropping 30 m arrives at about 23.6 m/s and the rider must brake it down to 5.4 m/s.

Only a parked trolley can be caught. A ridden trolley stays where it stopped, so a line cannot be ridden again until a death or a load re-parks every trolley. The cable is a cylinder, not a hold, so the player cannot take it by hand or hook. The Matron alone can go down a bare cable on her forearms.

Lines are entities 1800 + index, capped at kMaxLines = 24. The world makes exactly 24 add_line attempts: 1 yard line, 13 stack decks (levels 2-14) and 10 upper rings. A line that does not fit is not built.

The ground slingshot's pouch sits at (-3, 0.35, -55) in the yard, aim yaw 0 = -z, default elevation 1.431 rad (82 degrees). Two rubber bands of 10 kN/m with a 10.44 m natural length; draw up to 12 m at most 4 m/s; player power 200 kW at 88%; pouch force up to 160 kN. Tested: a 2.8 s draw stores over 200 kJ and throws the rider 240-275 m up at under 90 m/s, and with the chute opened over the tower it lands on the 220 ring. A 2.0 s draw throws at least 80 m lower.

Off the 220 ring's +z face, two 28.8 m pendulums share a 251.5 m axle at x -15: the rider's seat (pivot z -98.7) and a 235 kg ram held back. A kick on the trip (500 N) lets the ram strike the seat through a rubber buffer, and the seat rises to the 242 ring's edge (deck 242.25), held there by a ratchet. Action straps in, kicks and unbuckles; Drop leaves.

Two yard toys. The trapeze: a 30 kg bar on 7 m rods from (34, 12, -28); a 2.2 m launch stand west, a 5.0 m landing stand east; catch 0.2-1.2 m over the centre; Crouch pulls with up to 1500 N; grip 3 kN for 14 ticks. The pipe gallery: ten box pipes 1 m apart at y 4.6 from x 26.8 on lane z -34, a 1.5 m start stand, and a platform 4.7 m up at x 36.7-39.7. The monkey bars exist only in proving-ground worlds.
C7 on tower one's west face has a 5-pipe gallery at y 268.95 and an 8-pipe gallery, each pipe 0.3 m higher than the last at a 0.95 m pitch, from y 274.9. Brachiation can gain height bar by bar.

Wind exists only in two fixed boxes and always pushes -x (outward from the west face). Box one: x <= -26.6, y 262-300, z -166 to -128 (C7). Box two: x <= -12, y 788-830, z -197 to -178 (the summit's runway arm). Exposure ramps from 0 to 1 over the first 2 m (3 m at the summit). It does not grow with height, and there is no wind between the towers.

Wind speed is exposure*(4 + 12*gust), where gust = clamp(0.35 + 0.35 sin(2 pi t/7.3) + 0.3 sin(2 pi t/2.9 + 1), 0, 1) on the simulation clock, so it is deterministic. The push is 0.42*v^2 N on the body whenever it is not grounded: falling, under canopy, hanging, swinging or climbing. There is no separate canopy area, and neither the hook nor the zipline is pushed.
facts.numbers: 0.5*1.2*0.7 = 0.42; 4 m/s gives 6.7 N; 16 m/s gives 107.5 N = 1.26 m/s^2 on 85 kg; under a 9 m/s canopy drift is about 1.2 m/s

facts.claim: The summit deck (top 802.64) has a 38 m runway arm out of its west end to x = -50, centre line z -187.5, half-width 1.5, open at its end: run off it and open the parachute. Its end is 102.5 m (in z) from the second shaft's z = -290 face, at an x (-50) inside the shaft's -76..16 span.
facts.numbers: with the glide ratios above, crossing 102.5 m costs about 82 m of height off a flow run, 155 m off a walk

facts.claim: Left thumb: a floating stick (throw 150 units, 10% deadzone); pushing past 1.25x the throw forward latches sprint, held while forward stays at 0.5 or more. Right thumb: drag to look. In the gesture scheme a right-thumb flick of 10 mm within 0.15 s, 1.6x steeper than across, is the verb up or down. The stick pulled back hard within 0.14 s of pushing forward is a quick turn. Every touch is owned by one control from press to release.

The buttons are JUMP (reads CLIMB UP when hanging, JUMP OFF when climbing or swinging, THROW with stock in hand), ACTION (contextual), CROUCH (a toggle; SLIDE DOWN or HOLD ON on a climb), DROP and CHUTE (drawn in the same slot), HOOK (shown once had: tap fires, hold reels; label HOOK, ..., or REEL), TURN (buttons scheme only), CRANE and PAUSE. All but the reel fire on press.

A swipe up asks the native for its chosen up move. Hanging: climb up. On a bar: launch. On holds: top out, else jump off. In the air: wall kick, else trapeze catch, else a jump held for landing. Crouched: stand. On the ground, in order: throw, precision, springboard, vault or mantle, climb a hold, jump. Moves that let go or jump off (jump off, launch, let go, throw) are made only by a flick that lifts within 0.35 s.

A swipe down takes the first that applies: release the hook if out, pull on the trapeze, let go of a hang or bar, slide down a climb, set a load down, tuck in the air, lower into a hang from an edge close behind (moving under 1.5 m/s), slide at 5 m/s or more, else crouch. Hook release, let go and slide down need a flick that lifts within 0.35 s.

DROP lets go of the hook before anything else (hook, then slingshot, swing, trapeze, load, ledge or holds). DROP is shown whenever the hook is out. It precedes CHUTE in the hit order at the same slot, so a press there releases the hook first; CHUTE becomes pressable once DROP hides.

Keyboard: Space jump, E action, Q drop, F chute, G hook (held reels), R crane, C crouch toggle, Ctrl crouch held, Shift sprint. Pad: A jump, X action, B back, Y alt (chute in the air), right shoulder hook (held reels), right-stick click crouch, left-stick click sprint.

A save is the committed checkpoint only. It holds a format key, the tick, the checkpoint position and crouch, commit and death counts, the carried entity, the kit bodies' entity list and states, rope anchors, dogs, bins, latches, piles (up to 256), pools, cells, reels, the slingshot, swing and bay states, vertical controls and targets, grip loads and ratings, then fabricated objects. Corpses, the crew and the Matron's state are not written (a load sets her checkpoint to the default).

The key starts from 'SXCLIMB3' (0x5358434C494D4233) and is folded (key = key*1099511628211 ^ size) with sizeof Kit::BodyState, AnchorIndex, Kit::Pile, Slingshot::State, Swing::State, vertical::Command, JPH::RVec3 and Bay::State. Any change to those sizes changes the key, and every older save is refused.

A save loads only if its kit-body entity list equals the first N kit bodies of this world, in the same order. Bodies built since (built last) start as built. A body inserted, removed or moved earlier in the build order makes the save refused, and the presentation sets it aside as .bad and starts fresh. World solids and the native tower box are not kit bodies and are not in the save.

The kit is built in this order: bands, slingshot, swing, C6, vertical route, trapeze, pipe gallery, hook rack, vertical late, C7, wheel reload, summit, loose stock, forklifts, yard crane, deck forklifts, ziplines (with corpses), tower stock, crane steel, crane devices, machine weights, Matron throwables, then the bay, last. New saved bodies must come after the bay.

Jolt's contact sort was patched to key on entity ids (user data), so adding a body no longer perturbs distant simulations. A falsifier (scraperx_sim body order) builds the world with an extra box per band and requires every other result unchanged bit for bit.

The presentation writes user://climb.save when the commit or death count changed, at most every 2000 ms (at once when backgrounded or quitting), through a temp file and a rename. The beacon's lit state persists separately in user://summit.lit.

risks: The clear gap is far beyond one line. Tower one's stack outer face is z -176.3 (OuterEdgeBeam) and the second shaft's most proud relief is z -286.9 (FaceDuct), about 110 m apart, against a 30 m line whose reach shrinks with height difference. No single hook shot, hook swing (60 m same height, about 102 m only by dropping 30 m) or jump crosses it. A crossing needs intermediate holds, a line of the code's own kind, or a fall that is honestly a fall.

Tower two has zero bitable or climbable holds today. Every relief box is 1.2 m or more in its thinnest dimension. Any hook or hand play there needs new Box-shaped members with sections of 0.18 m or less, on static or 400 kg+ bodies; cylinders never count.

The parachute is a universal, instant recovery and a crossing tool: no opening delay, about 4 m of height enough to survive at 30 m/s, and a forward glide equal to the take-off speed (up to 8.9 m/s off flow). From the summit runway arm (802.64 m, 102.5 m from the shaft face) a player can glide to tower two now. Gated first access through tower one must survive this, and so must 'falls are the price' designs.

Aiming the hook on touch is very tight: about 0.3-0.65 degrees across a thin hold at 30 m, a 2.8 m gravity drop to aim over, no trajectory or bite preview (reticle dot only), and gyro off by default. The touch tests set yaw and pitch directly rather than aiming with a thumb.

A slack line catches with a jolt. The bite fixes the line at the bite distance; moving toward the anchor (running, jumping) makes slack, and a fall caught at about 6.7 m/s or more along the line tears the hook out. The hook therefore cannot arrest a real fall unless the line was taut or the motion was across it. Holding REEL takes up slack instantly.

Pendulum arcs are lethal at speed. The bottom of a 30 m swing runs at about 24 m/s, and any side-on contact at 10 m/s or more kills, so a swing must meet structure near its apex or along it. A release landing 30 m lower arrives at 18.3 m/s down: alive, but with a broken ankle unless prepared or rolled.

After a hook release, holding the stick brakes the fling toward the last ground air_full_speed_ (at least 5.5 m/s) at 14 m/s^2, because stow_hook does not update it. Bar and zipline releases do update it. Designs that rely on flinging off the hook must expect players to hold the stick.

If the canopy is left open, its drag slows a hook swing (it applies whenever outside a traversal). The UI's DROP/CHUTE shared slot and the swipe-down priority (hook release first) mean that, with the hook out, the down swipe and that slot always let go of the hook. A player on the line cannot crouch, tuck or open the chute from that slot without releasing first.

Reeling holds the HOOK button with the right thumb, the same thumb that looks and aims. Dragging off the button turns the touch into look and stops the reel. Pumping is on the left stick at only 160 N.

A zipline is one ride per life (the trolley stays at the bottom until a death or load), cannot be grabbed by hand or hook, must descend, and needs braking to 5.4 m/s or less at the buffer. A long inter-tower line arrives at over 20 m/s unbraked and tears the rider into the post. A return or reuse route by zipline is not possible without new code.

The zipline budget may be full. kMaxLines is 24 and the world makes 24 add_line attempts. Adding a line inside the existing sequence also shifts every later kit body (stock, devices, weights, throwables, bay), and every old save is refused. A new line must be built after the bay, and only if a slot is free.

Saves refuse any reordering. New kit bodies (machines, static kit frames, ziplines) must be built after the bay, the current last kit body. Changing the size of a saved state struct (Bay::State, Swing::State, Slingshot::State, Kit::BodyState and so on) changes the format key and refuses every save. World solids are not saved, but adding them can still drift fixed-input tests (see the test-drift skill and the body-order falsifier).

Checkpoints come from geometry, not placement. Any firm standable surface on tower two (a ledge, a beam top) becomes the restore point the instant the player stands on it, outside a traversal. Designers must make sure every standable spot has a non-lethal way on (or at least the chute).
There is no hang stamina. A hang is held forever unless the load spikes, so 'finite grip' pressure must come from something else (wind, a machine, the Matron, loads).
Wind does not exist between the towers and does not grow with height. It is two fixed -x boxes, and adding wind to the crossing means a new zone in apply_wind and new tuning constants.

The landing death rule reads the world vertical speed only. Landing on a moving deck, or arriving fast horizontally, is judged on vertical speed alone. Fast horizontal arrivals are judged by the side-on hit rule (10 m/s) against walls, and by long runouts at reduced traction after a heavy landing.

Compass words in the code are inconsistent. The yard and start (+z) are called 'south' and the stack decks call -z 'north' (Deck8North at z -170), but the Deck154 spawn's 'north band' (z -128.2), Matron::kRingNorthZ = -126.91 and the hook rack's 'north-west corner' comment (physics_world.cpp:244) all name the +z side 'north', and probes.cpp:797 calls the same rack 'south band'. Designers should work in coordinates.
The hook cannot be fired from a hang, climb, bar or zipline (it needs traversal None). Hook-to-hold-to-hook chains need a moment of free flight or standing between holds.
The hook bites only at tick ends or on contact. At 40 m/s it moves 0.44 m a tick, so a near pass beside a thin hold that does not touch it can miss unless it ends a tick within 0.16 m.
unknowns: How many of the 24 zipline add_line attempts actually build in the current world. This needs a run (Simulation::zipline_count()), so whether a free line slot exists is unverified.

What the hook body does when it reaches the 30 m line end without a bite (rebound against the rope, whether it can still bite on the rebound) has not been measured. Only the 2.5 s miss timer is certain.

The tear threshold of about 6.7 m/s along the line assumes the rope constraint removes the radial speed in one tick. RopeConstraint's actual compliance (src/sim/rope_constraint.cpp) was not read, and the code comment says 'about 2.5 m' of free fall.
The ledge-catch tear threshold for a horizontal arrival is not measured. The code gives only vertical catches: 1 m holds, 6 m (10.9 m/s) tears.

The precision-jump comment says 'a standing precision reaches ~1.5 m', while the code's 3 m/s push over the jump's flight time gives 2.5-3.4 m. The source of the difference (for example an edge or landing check) was not traced.
Whether a climbing body (gravity off, velocity set each tick) being pulled by a reeling or taut hook line triggers the traversal stall abort (an error over 0.22 m for 12 ticks) has not been tested.

Whether Kit::restore re-places static kit bodies from saved states (that is, whether moving a static kit body's build position affects old saves beyond the order check) was not read in mechanism_kit.cpp.
Whether the presentation lets the hook fire while carrying a load. The native does not refuse it (hook_pre_step does not check the carry).
Effective pendulum carry with the 160 N pump, line bends, and players holding the stick has not been simulated. The figures given are for an ideal pendulum.
Whether any existing touch test drives hook aiming by real thumb drags (the ones read set _yaw and _pitch directly).
The Matron's reach to the second tower. Nothing in matron.cpp was read about levels above 286 or other structures; her levels are listed as the 154 m deck, 13 stack decks and 10 rings.

The summit is one static kit frame (entity 1900, laid out about (-20, 800, -187.5)). Its deck spans x -12..11.5, z -191.5..-183.5, top 802.64 m. 'Lit' means this: a 300 kg striker plate on four guides, held up by 5 kN of strut preload, latches the lamp lit for good once it travels 0.2 m down. The summit is not an ending. Standing on the derrick's upper receiver (entity 1978) latches summit_reached once, and the HUD shows the toast 'THE TOP' with height, time and falls. Lighting the lamp shows 'THE LIGHT IS ON / SEEN FROM THE GROUND. NOW GET DOWN.' and play continues. No credits or end state exist; what stands at the top is left to the owner, and AS-015 ('stand on 800.00 m') is UNAUTHORED.

facts.claim: Her states: Dormant, Straining, Emerging, Hunting, Searching, Shuffling, Dead, Guarding, Peering, Unrigging, Staggering, Down. Loud noise carrying 30 m to the locker wakes her; she strains 16 s, emerges in 2.2 s, then hunts by sound.

Her speeds and senses: shuffle 1.0 m/s, search 2.4, hunt 6.8 (the player walks 5.5 and sprints 8); a catch is her hands within 0.85 m; sight 9 m with a clear line; a sound of full loudness carries 55 m.

The levels she can hunt are all on tower one: her 154 deck, the 176 ring, ten rings above it (198.25-396.25 m, 'with no way up of hers known'), the 13 stack decks (11-143 m) and the bay's bracket. Nothing above 396.25 m or off tower one is in her world.

How she changes level: she clings to any floor that moves under her (cages), at any stage; frail, she cannot cross a gap wider than 0.45 m and never walks off an edge; in the Turn she leaps gaps up to 3 m, climbs her ladder 154->176 and goes down zipline cables on her forearms; she knows the 143->154 riser but never takes hold of it; her corner pipe links only 132-154 m, and only once she is past the pest stage.

Her stages (Pest, Dangerous, Changed) follow a rage fed only by sound at her ear. Only fully changed are her hands a death; before that they shove (5.5 m/s along the floor, 2 up), and dangerous she aims the shove at the shaft's rim within 3 m.

Her hoard, as built: as a pest she takes light stock (25 kg or less) the player has handled and throws it at 7.5 m/s from 2.5-6 m; unable to throw, she carries it to her post (-10.3, -129.0) on her deck and drops it there (native 'matron hoard'). The 'hoard' where echoes of looked-at things appear is her chart's step 2, not built.

Her trap at the bay on her deck: with the player across the bay from her, she drops onto a bracket and holds the walkway leaf on her palms (about 930 N) as bait. A climber who steps on it falls 11 m to the 143 deck. The chain hooked onto the leaf beats the trap. She sets it at most three times a run.

The only thing that kills her is a fall: her deck's catwalk plates shear under her stamping load (bolt 2.1 kN averaged over 0.25 s), and more than 12 m below her floor counts as dead, for good. A restore puts her back at her locker at the saved stage; nothing teleports her, and her route is a fixed rule over walkways.

Plan section 2.1: every stage states receiver, transfer, transmission, source, player access (bounded effort <= 150 N over <= 0.3 m) and persistence and retry before code; 'No hidden stubs, remote attachments, completion flags or pose snapping.'

Plan section 2.2: the main motion lasts about 5-15 s; one or two player actions per stage; a stage's output is 'a stable support, bridge, stair or ride the player can use and leave; no mandatory launches across a gap'; no compulsory carrying ahead of a gravity event.

Plan section 2.5: proven means the native falsifiers pass (no source, no motion; no link, no motion; the ledger closes; the rest matrix holds; the swept path is clear), the stage is played through the game's input from the game's start, and CI builds the APK only after.
Rule 1, no link no lift: a machine's stored energy stays stored until the player completes the chain. A machine may run on its own power, its motor finite and rated.
Rules 2-4: energy pays for height, checked every tick; every link is physical (contact, constraint or force), with any simplified model declared; rides are moving supports.

Rule 5: the parachute is the way back. Nothing is designed only to keep a player from getting stuck, but a player who spends or wrecks a machine must have 'some way to fix it or to go on (a re-arm, another route, or the canopy down to try again), never a dead save'.

Rules 6-8: every part is held by visible structure and handled parts are marked hazard or yellow; climbs are designed and never bypass the machine below; easy paths (stair, ladder, walkway) are only the plainer, slower backup beside each stage.

Rule 9, nothing repeats: each new stage brings an action, form and look no earlier stage has, and its record names that action. The hanging handle grabbed and stepped back from 'is spent' (about twenty machines, S1 to O); kit parts may be reused, encounters may not.

Rule 10, determinism: the same state and inputs give the same final state bit for bit; no randomness, clock time or frame-rate dependence in the simulation (90 Hz fixed); checked by the native 'determinism' test.

Rule 11, not chutes and ladders: no new ladder on the route (only as the rule-8 backup) and no lift that starts when the player pulls something. A few existing ladders and pulls may stay; ladders get replaced, never working machines, which may at most change how they start.
Rule 12: fill the gaps with machines for one unbroken route from grade. The summit is at 800 m; 'the top is left open; the tower is not cut down until the owner decides'.

Rule 13, irresistible at first sight: its open work includes 'shortcuts that reward breaking the intended route, because the physics allows them', the height felt, pressure from the world, something RELEASED after a build-up that chases the player (deterministic), and 'a reason to reach the top, visible from the ground'. How a native test is written: all tests build into one executable, scraperx_sim_tests, from tests/sim_tests_*.cpp listed in CMakeLists.txt. Each group is a run_X() declared in tests/sim_tests.hpp and called in tests/simulation_tests.cpp, both under SCRAPERX_ONLY=<group> and in the full run. Tests build Simulation s(InitialSpawn::...), drive it with helpers (walk_to, hold_stick, c4_mantle, c4_hang_up) and check with require(); they print 'PASS scraperx_sim ...' lines, which CI greps from a fixed list.

How a touch scenario is registered: add 'name': <InitialSpawn int> to SCENARIOS, a match arm in _run(), and the scenario function in one of the family files. The inheritance chain is ui_test_driver -> ui_test_uncanny -> ui_test_act -> ui_test_chase -> ui_test_stack -> ui_test_service -> ui_test_rides -> ui_test_bands -> ui_test_moves -> ui_test_base -> Node. A touch_ run fails if the swipes and flicks recognized differ from those injected; a '_buttons' suffix replays it on the BUTTONS scheme.
